quick: 250-500 mg q6h oral; 250 mg-1 g (up to 2 g) q4-6h IM/IV
Empty stomach: 1 h before or 2 h after food
Excreted in milk; use with caution
Reduce dose only in severe impairment
Renal, hepatic, hematologic on prolonged use
summary: Cloxacillin is a penicillinase-resistant (anti-staphylococcal) isoxazolyl penicillin used primarily for infections caused by penicillinase-producing, methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. It is acid-stable and orally absorbed but should be taken on an empty stomach, and is also available for IM and IV use in more serious infections. Like other penicillins it is bactericidal through inhibition of bacterial cell-wall synthesis; the bulky isoxazolyl side chain protects the beta-lactam ring from staphylococcal penicillinase. It is inactive against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and has limited activity against most gram-negative organisms and enterococci. The principal risk is penicillin hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis, with rare reports of cholestatic hepatitis.
indications: Infections due to penicillinase-producing (methicillin-susceptible) Staphylococcus aureus
Skin and soft-tissue infections (cellulitis, abscess, wound infections)
Bone and joint infections (osteomyelitis, septic arthritis)
Mixed infections with susceptible streptococci where staphylococcal cover is needed

dosage.d: 250 mg-1 g (up to 2 g) every 4-6 hours
dosage.n: IV by slow injection or infusion for severe/deep infections
High parenteral doses; consider combination therapy

dosage.d: 25-50 mg/kg/day (up to 100 mg/kg/day in severe infection) divided every 6 hours

admin: Take oral doses on an empty stomach, at least 1 h before or 2 h after meals, with a full glass of water
Give in equally spaced doses to maintain consistent serum levels
Administer IV by slow injection over 3-4 minutes or by infusion; give IM by deep intramuscular injection
Continue therapy for at least 48-72 h after the patient becomes asymptomatic; treat deep infections for longer courses
Screen for penicillin/cephalosporin allergy before starting; confirm methicillin-susceptible (not MRSA) target organism
moa: Cloxacillin inhibits bacterial cell-wall biosynthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), blocking transpeptidation and cross-linking of peptidoglycan in actively dividing organisms, producing a bactericidal effect. Its bulky isoxazolyl side chain sterically protects the beta-lactam ring from hydrolysis by staphylococcal penicillinase (beta-lactamase), giving it activity against penicillinase-producing, methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus that resist benzylpenicillin and aminopenicillins. It is inactive against MRSA, in which an altered PBP2a confers resistance, and has poor activity against most gram-negative bacteria and enterococci.

absolute: History of serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to cloxacillin or other beta-lactams
relative: History of cephalosporin or multiple-allergen sensitivity
Infectious mononucleosis / EBV (high rash incidence with penicillins)
Severe renal impairment without dose adjustment
monitor: Neonates and elderly on high doses

preg: There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Penicillins, including cloxacillin, are generally regarded as having a good safety record in pregnancy, but use only if clearly needed and benefit justifies any potential risk.
lact: Cloxacillin is excreted in breast milk in small amounts and may sensitize the infant or cause diarrhoea, candidiasis or rash. It is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding but use with caution and monitor the infant.
renal: Cloxacillin is eliminated by both renal and biliary routes and is highly protein-bound, so it accumulates less than aminopenicillins. No dose reduction is needed in mild-to-moderate impairment; reduce the dose or extend the interval only in severe renal impairment (e.g. CrCl <10 mL/min). It is not significantly removed by haemodialysis, so no supplemental post-dialysis dose is required.
hepatic: Cholestatic hepatitis and hepatic dysfunction, sometimes delayed in onset, have rarely been reported, particularly with high parenteral doses and prolonged therapy. Use with caution and monitor liver function in patients with hepatic impairment or on extended courses. Contraindicated if there is a prior history of cloxacillin-associated cholestatic jaundice.

major: Allopurinol - increased incidence of skin rash
Methotrexate - penicillins may reduce renal clearance, raising methotrexate toxicity
moderate: Probenecid - decreases renal tubular secretion of cloxacillin, raising and prolonging serum levels
Oral anticoagulants (warfarin) - possible altered anticoagulant effect; monitor INR
minor: Oral contraceptives - possible reduced efficacy; advise backup contraception
Bacteriostatic antibiotics (tetracyclines, chloramphenicol, macrolides) - may antagonize bactericidal effect of penicillins in vitro
interactions.food: Food markedly reduces absorption; take on an empty stomach at least 1 h before or 2 h after meals.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction (Clinitest) tests; use enzymatic glucose-oxidase methods. Periodic renal, hepatic and haematological evaluation advised on prolonged high-dose therapy.

serious: Severe cutaneous reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS, exfoliative dermatitis)
rare: Cholestatic hepatitis / hepatic dysfunction (may be delayed)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (airway swelling, hypotension) - treat with epinephrine

monitoring: Renal, hepatic and haematopoietic function periodically on prolonged or high-dose therapy
Liver function in patients with hepatic impairment or on extended parenteral courses
Allergic reactions, especially early after the first dose
Local reactions (phlebitis, injection-site pain) with parenteral use
counsel: Take on an empty stomach (1 h before or 2 h after food) with a full glass of water; complete the entire course
Report rash, hives, swelling, mucosal lesions or breathing difficulty immediately
Report watery or bloody diarrhea, which may occur during or weeks after treatment
Maintain evenly spaced doses around the clock for best effect
Use additional contraception if on hormonal contraceptives
pk: Bactericidal soon after absorption during active bacterial multiplication
Oral peak ~1 hour; ~7-15 mcg/mL after a 500 mg oral dose
Store capsules at 20-25 C (68-77 F); refrigerate reconstituted syrup and discard after 14 days; use reconstituted parenteral solution promptly
pearls: NOT FDA-approved or marketed in the US (the US anti-staphylococcal oral analogue is dicloxacillin); this record is authored from EMA/BNF/Martindale/Indian NF pharmacology rather than an openFDA label
Penicillinase-resistant: drug of choice for methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) but inactive against MRSA
Highly protein-bound (~90-95%) and partly biliary-excreted, so accumulates less in renal failure than aminopenicillins
Food markedly reduces oral absorption - always dose on an empty stomach
Narrow gram-positive spectrum: poor activity against most gram-negative organisms and enterococci
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule; do not double the dose.
overdose: In overdose, discontinue the drug and treat symptomatically with supportive measures; gastrointestinal symptoms and fluid/electrolyte imbalance may occur, and very high doses (especially parenteral with renal impairment) may rarely cause neurotoxicity/seizures. Cloxacillin is highly protein-bound and is not appreciably removed by haemodialysis.
